name: IN-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Messmer running with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 3%
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean, Messmer's incumbency, and his roughly four-to-one fundraising advantage over Mary Allen all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and prediction markets agree at about 96% for the GOP. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, there is no basis to move the forecast.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected incumbent stumble could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Indiana's 8th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with an 18-point Republican advantage in recent partisan performance. First-term incumbent Mark Messmer is running for reelection after clearing his primary, and he holds a decisive financial edge, having raised about $1.17 million to Democrat Mary Allen's roughly $295,000. No outside groups have reported spending in the race, and no public general-election polls are available.

Prediction markets give Messmer about a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The forecast expects Messmer to win by roughly 17 points, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling and the possibility of an unusual late-cycle shift in the environment.
